SBP:
Do you tell the program director or CCC chair about difficult behavior in your didactic?
In general, the answer should be “yes”.
The PD (and maybe the CCC) need to know if patterns of behavior are emerging for any one resident - they are uniquely positioned to have this perspective.
If this is an isolated incident, they will likely not do anything further with the information.
If this is a pattern of behavior, or is an egregious act, the resident may need some more dedicated coaching from the program.
If it is a personal issue (sick family member, etc), I encourage the learner to tell their PD, and offer to support them in any way they would like.
ICS: Begin with “I’m on your side.” Emphasize motivation to help them improve. Often, this starts well before the conversation begins and extends to your entire relationship with the resident

Advocacy is stating something that you noticed. This is the “O” from the SOAP Process.
Inquiry is telling the learner your concerns about it and asking for their thoughts.
Be inquisitive. Either from a single advocacy inquiry statement or may require more “digging” to actually “get to the root of” why it is happening.
PBLI:
Assessment. Clarify if resident truly is at the level perceived (are they covering for deficits?).
Find out what they are currently doing to learn emergency medicine
Emphasize the difference between clinical knowledge and boards/In-training exam knowledge (can be strong in one area and not the other)

Co-create a study plan.
Have the learner first suggest ways they think they could improve their medical knowledge.
Be specific. Have the learner pick a reading material and include chapters to cover.
Create a deadline. Use a calendar to outline curriculum keeping in mind the rotations of the learner.
Modify the plan as needed. Learners are more likely to be successful if they came up with the solution.
Accountability. Schedule time for check-ins and commit to placing in calendar.
Evaluation. Use various modalities for assessment. (e.g. Rosh review, question banks, etc.)
Celebrate mini-successes.

Testing effect/retrieval practice (for those already reading/listening to podcasts/etc.
Creating flashcards then testing themselves
Creating mini-lectures/1-minute presentations and encourage teaching junior learners.
